## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sasitthaka Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 56) is a training rule in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka regulating proper conduct and etiquette regarding the disposal of bowl-rinsing water containing grains of boiled rice [SuttaCentral]. On SuttaCentral, it is titled *Sasitthaka* and translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali as "Discarding waste water with rice" [SuttaCentral]. None of the secondary literature excerpts located in the reference dossier pertain to this Vinaya text, as all instances of "SK 56" refer instead to verse 56 of the classical philosophical work *Sāṃkhyakārikā*.
This training rule is widely attested across Buddhist monastic traditions. Curated parallels on SuttaCentral document corresponding rules in the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Pātimokkhas of the Theravāda, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages extant in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan, as well as the Theravāda Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. In addition, DharmaNexus records 298 internal Pali matches across 99 texts, reflecting extensive shared procedural and contextual phraseology throughout the Vinaya; its closest alignment is with the preceding Sekhiya rule 55 (sharing §1.4–1.26), with substantial reuse also found in Sekhiya 37, Sekhiya 1, Sekhiya 57, and the Bhesajjakkhandhaka (Kd 6) [DharmaNexus].
